limits: THE `unparseable` VERDICT NOW HAS REGISTERED CASES; the policy collision that previously blocked them was resolved AT THE RULE SITE (issue #1180). It used to read: a fixture for this verdict must be unparseable BY CONSTRUCTION, while pyproject.toml's ruff config excluded only `controls/*/anchors` under the sentence "anchors are not linted. Fixtures are." A fixture that cannot lint and a policy that requires fixtures to lint cannot both hold, and `make lint` reported 4 syntax errors with a case present. A fixture-local `.ruff.toml` would have worked and was REFUSED, because it takes the exception while leaving the sentence at the policy site reading true and being false. THE RESOLUTION WAS TO CORRECT THE SENTENCE: pyproject.toml now excludes the two unparseable fixture FILES BY NAME - never a directory or a glob, so the next unparseable fixture added by accident is still caught - and the comment at that rule site states what is actually true. tests/test_negative_controls.py::test_the_ruff_fixture_exclusions_have_not_grown pins the exclude list's exact membership, so widening it is a deliberate edit to a red test rather than a quiet extra line. WHAT THE TWO CASES EACH DISCRIMINATE, because two were needed and one would not do: `unknown-unparseable-with-violation` is the #1180 UNION - a real unwaived violation beside a file that does not parse. Before the fix the gate printed the UNKNOWN refusal AND the detection marker over this tree, both manifest patterns matched one output, and the harness `_ambiguous()` scored it UNRESOLVED. It fails if a future change lets `detect_signal` win, because the observation would then be BAD against a registered UNKNOWN. `unknown-unparseable-neighbour` is the UNEARNED GREEN - a fully compliant fixture beside a file that does not parse. It fails on the bare `except SyntaxError: continue` guard, which prints `ok - ...` for that tree because `files_scanned` counts a file that was never opened; the observation would be GOOD against a registered UNKNOWN. The first distinguishes a refusal from a detection, the second distinguishes a refusal from a clean bill, and no single case does both. WHY THE REFUSAL CARRIES `unknown_signal` AND NOT THE DETECTION MARKER (counter-model review, 2026-09-21, codex/gpt-6-astra). The first version of the unparseable verdict deliberately ENDED its line in this gate's own "nothing was scanned" idiom so `detect_signal` would match it with no regex change - reasoning about the detector's COVERAGE, and missing what the match MEANS. `detect_signal` is how the harness scores a SUCCESSFUL DETECTION, so a parse refusal was counted as the gate catching its planted defect: a case whose NEIGHBOURING file merely failed to parse earned `BAD` even when the planted violation was silently waived, and the control could no longer distinguish detecting our defect from failing to examine a neighbour's. That is detector-contracts question 2 breaking inside the instrument built to answer it, introduced by the fix for a defect of the same class. The refusal carries #1129's `unknown_signal` marker, checked BEFORE `detect_signal`, and deliberately avoids the words "nothing was scanned" - that phrase would still match `detect_signal`'s second alternative and re-create the collision one layer down, precedence or not. The disjointness is pinned in BOTH directions by tests/test_negative_fixture_preconditions.py::test_a_parse_refusal_is_not_scored_as_a_detection, and on their UNION by ::test_a_mixed_tree_resolves_to_exactly_one_verdict_marker - both read the patterns out of THIS file rather than hardcoding them, so editing either signal without re-checking the pairing fails there. The union test exists because the two-state test passed throughout: it checked each condition separately and never their combination, and an independent verification reproduced the same separate checks and missed it too. WHAT THE EARLIER WITHDRAWN CASE ESTABLISHED, recorded because it was OBSERVED and would otherwise be lost: the framework tells a CRASHING gate from a DETECTING one (the #946 property) on this gate's own anchor. Pre-fix, `survey_paths` re-parsed unguarded and died with an uncaught SyntaxError, exiting 1 - the same exit code a real detection produces. With the case registered, anchor eae94b5 nonetheless read `missed the known-bad input (blind, as required)`, because the harness keys on `detect_signal` and a traceback emits none. An exit-code-only harness would have scored that crash as a successful detection and the anchor as sighted. STILL NOT COVERED BY A CASE: the gate's per-file scope limits (an assertion lifted into a helper, and assertion ORDER) are stated in the success message and exercised only by tests/test_negative_fixture_preconditions.py, not by a registered case.

cases.name: unknown-unparseable-with-violation
cases.anchor_expect_reason: same structural blindness as unknown-unparseable-neighbour - no survey, no refusal branch - and here it is doubly unearned: this tree also holds a real unwaived wholesale PATH replacement in the PARSEABLE file, which the anchor misses because it predates #933's dict-literal shape (the same blindness that makes it miss bad-dictliteral, as recorded above). So its `ok` (exit 0) rests both on a file it never parsed and on a finding it cannot see. Making it agree would require giving it both the survey and the later shape, at which point it would stop being blind to bad-dictliteral and this control would lose its anchor.

cases.name: unknown-unparseable-neighbour
cases.anchor_expect_reason: this anchor is the older reader and has NO survey and NO refusal branch at all (measured: zero occurrences of `unparseable`, `UNKNOWN` or `files_scanned` in anchors/eae94b5-check-negative-fixture-preconditions.py), so it cannot represent "a file here was not examined" in any form. It tolerates the unparseable neighbour by contributing no findings for it and then renders `ok - every constructed absence asserts its precondition` (exit 0) over a population it never established. That unearned clean bill IS the blindness under test; an anchor able to refuse here would have to derive the population, and would then no longer be the frozen reader this control pins.
